newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Indian quarantine unchanged for Australian wheat.
newsitem.headline: Indian quarantine unchanged for Australian wheat.

text.p: India will not impose changed quarantine restrictions on the import of one million tonnes of Australian wheat, Australian officials said on Friday.
The one million tonnes to be shipped later this year is covered by an agreement reached in recent days between the AWB and India which settles a long running dispute.
The dispute was over Indian claims that Australian exports of wheat contained weed seeds.
However, India would accept the one million tonnes without any change to earlier quarantine and inspection arrangements, Australian Wheat Board (AWB) officials told Reuters.

Analysts have noted that Indian complaints about weed seed in the Australian shipments followed falling prices in international wheat markets. India last year contracted to buy 2.3 million tonnes of Australian wheat in 1997.
Shipments were haltered after deliveries of 1.3 million tonnes. The new shipment schedule calls for the shipment of 250,000 tonnes in August/September and 750,000 tonnes in November/December.
Nigel Officer, general manager international of the AWB, told Reuters earlier there had been a "resolution in a commercial manner."
India is expected to be in the market for more imported wheat this year.
